function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: The unit of measurement for the command execution time, such as 'seconds' or 'milliseconds'

message.reasoning: The user wants to set a timer for 10 seconds using the timeout command. They say "You should use timeout 10." So they want to run a command that waits 10 seconds. On Windows, the timeout command is used like "timeout /t 10". But they said "timeout 10". That might be Linux? In Linux, "timeout 10" would run a command for 10 seconds? Actually "timeout" in Linux is part of coreutils: "timeout DURATION COMMAND". So "timeout 10" alone is incomplete. But maybe they want to just run "timeout 10" which will wait 10 seconds and then exit? In Linux, "timeout 10" will exit immediately because no command given. But maybe they want to run "timeout 10" to wait 10 seconds. Let's interpret: They want to run a command that sets a timer for 10 seconds. We can use the function to execute a system command. We'll call cmd_controller_execute with command "timeout 10" and unit "seconds". But we need to specify the command exactly. The function expects a string. We'll pass "timeout 10". The unit param is optional. We'll set unit to "seconds". That will run the command. Let's do that.
